ai.literal: Wisdom is a tool protecting from ruin, and an inner fortress impossible to destroy even for enemies.
ai.translation: Wisdom is an armor that wards off ruin; it is an inner fortress that even enemies cannot destroy.
ai.modern: அறிவு என்பது அழிவு வராமல் காக்கும் கருவியாகும்; அது பகைவர்களாலும் உள்ளே புகுந்து அழிக்க முடியாத ஒரு கோட்டையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines wisdom using two powerful metaphors: an active tool and a passive defense. First, wisdom acts as a tool (கருவி) that prevents ruin (அற்றம்) before it can strike. Second, it functions as an inner fortress (அரண்) built within the mind. While physical fortresses can be breached by hostile forces, this mental fortress is so secure that even the most determined enemies (செறுவார்) cannot penetrate or destroy it.

ai.literal: Not letting (the mind) go in the path it went, avoiding evil, and directing it towards goodness is wisdom.
ai.translation: Wisdom consists in not letting the mind wander wherever it desires, but restraining it from evil and directing it towards the path of goodness.
ai.modern: மனம் போன போக்கிலே அதைச் செல்ல விடாமல், தீமையிலிருந்து விலக்கி, நன்மையான வழியில் செலுத்துவதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the active discipline and control of the mind. The mind naturally tends to wander in the direction of sensory desires and impulses. Wisdom does not allow the mind to run free in these directions, but instead restrains it from harmful paths and steers it toward what is good and virtuous. Thus, wisdom is not merely intellectual capacity, but the practical mastery of one's thoughts and actions.

ai.literal: Whatever thing, from whosoever's mouth one hears, of that thing, the true substance to discern is wisdom.
ai.translation: To discern the true substance of whatever is heard, from whomsoever it is heard, is wisdom.
ai.modern: எந்தக் கருத்தை யார் யார் சொல்லக் கேட்டாலும், அக்கருத்தின் உண்மையான பொருளைக் கண்டறிவதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core nature of true wisdom. In daily life, we receive information, advice, and opinions from many different people. Wisdom does not lie in blindly accepting or rejecting a statement based on the status, authority, or identity of the speaker. Instead, a wise person looks past the speaker's mouth (வாய்) and analyzes the statement itself to find its objective, underlying truth (மெய்ப்பொருள்).

ai.literal: Speaking so that complex matters become easy to understand and penetrate the listener's mind, and oneself discerning the subtle meaning from the mouth of others, is wisdom.
ai.translation: Wisdom is speaking so clearly that complex ideas easily penetrate the minds of others, while being able to discern the subtle, deep truths in whatever others say.
ai.modern: தான் சொல்லும் கருத்துக்களைக் கேட்பவர் மனதில் எளிதாகப் பதியுமாறு விளக்கிச் சொல்வதும், பிறர் பேசும்போது அவர்களுடைய சொற்களிலிருந்து நுட்பமான உண்மைகளைக் கண்டறிந்து கொள்வதும் அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the two-way nature of wise communication. First, when speaking, a wise person simplifies complex ideas so that they easily enter and settle in the listener's mind. Second, when listening, even if others speak vaguely or poorly, a wise person possesses the sharp intellect to extract the deep, subtle truth hidden in their words. Thus, true wisdom lies in making oneself easily understood while effortlessly understanding the deeper meaning of others.

ai.literal: To embrace the world is wisdom; that which has neither expanding nor contracting is true wisdom.
ai.translation: To live in harmony with the world is wisdom; true wisdom is to remain equanimous, free from both elation and depression.
ai.modern: உலகத்தோடு பொருந்தி வாழ்வதே சிறந்த அறிவாகும்; இன்ப துன்பங்களால் மன விரிவோ அல்லது மனச் சுருக்கமோ அடையாமல் சமமாக இருப்பதே உண்மையான அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines wisdom through two key concepts: harmony and equanimity. First, 'ஒட்பம்' (mental clarity) is shown as 'உலகம் தழீஇயது', which means embracing and living in harmony with the people of the world. Second, true 'அறிவு' (wisdom) is described as having neither 'மலர்தல்' (expanding or blooming with joy/elation) nor 'கூம்பல்' (contracting or closing with grief/depression). A truly wise person maintains a steady, balanced mind regardless of changing fortunes.

ai.literal: In whichever way dwells the world, with the world in that same way to dwell is wisdom.
ai.translation: To live in harmony with the world, adapting to the way the world lives, is true wisdom.
ai.modern: உலகம் எத்தகைய வழியில் வாழ்கிறதோ, அந்த உலகத்தோடு பொருந்தி அதே வழியில் வாழ்வதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines wisdom not as isolated intellectual knowledge, but as the practical ability to adapt and live in harmony with society. The word 'உலகம்' (world) here refers to the wise and noble people of the world. 'எவ்வது உறைவது' means 'in whichever way they live', and 'அவ்வது உறைவது' means 'living in that very same manner'. True wisdom ('அறிவு') lies in conforming to the righteous customs and conduct of the community rather than standing apart in stubborn isolation.

ai.literal: Those who possess wisdom know what will happen; those who lack wisdom are those who cannot know that.
ai.translation: Those who possess wisdom foresee what is to come; those who lack wisdom are incapable of knowing it.
ai.modern: அறிவு உடையவர்கள் எதிர்காலத்தில் நடக்கப் போவதை அறிவார்கள்; அறிவு இல்லாதவர்கள் அதனை அறிய இயலாதவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the capacity for foresight. The word 'āva-tu' refers to that which is yet to happen, meaning future events or the consequences of current actions. Wise people can anticipate these outcomes and act proactively. Conversely, those who lack wisdom are described as being completely unable to perceive or prepare for what lies ahead.

ai.literal: Not fearing that which is to be feared is foolishness; fearing that which is to be feared is the action of those who know.
ai.translation: Not to fear what ought to be feared is folly; to fear what ought to be feared is the way of the wise.
ai.modern: அஞ்ச வேண்டியதற்கு அஞ்சாமல் இருப்பது அறியாமை ஆகும்; அஞ்ச வேண்டியதற்கு அஞ்சுவதே அறிவுடையோரின் செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the relationship between wisdom and fear. It states that failing to fear things that genuinely deserve fear, such as moral evils or destructive dangers, is a sign of ignorance. True wisdom does not lie in blind, reckless courage. Instead, recognizing what is truly harmful and acting with a healthy, protective fear toward it is the characteristic behavior of those who possess knowledge.

ai.literal: For those with wisdom who guard against that which is to come beforehand, there is not any affliction that comes to make them tremble.
ai.translation: For those possessing the wisdom to guard against future events beforehand, there is no calamity that can come to make them tremble.
ai.modern: வரப்போகும் துன்பத்தை முன்னதாகவே அறிந்து காத்துக் கொள்ளும் அறிவுடையவர்களுக்கு, அவர்கள் நடுங்கும்படி வரக்கூடிய துன்பம் எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of foresight and prevention. The phrase 'எதிரதாக் காக்கும்' describes the act of anticipating future dangers and taking protective measures before they arrive. Those who possess this active wisdom ('அறிவினார்க்') are never caught off guard. Consequently, no sudden calamity ('நோய்') can ever come to shock or shake ('அதிர') them, as they are always prepared.

ai.literal: Those who possess wisdom possess everything; those who lack wisdom, what even if they possess, they have nothing.
ai.translation: Those who possess wisdom possess everything; those who lack wisdom, whatever else they may possess, possess nothing at all.
ai.modern: அறிவு உடையவர்கள் எல்லாவற்றையும் உடையவர்கள் ஆவர்; அறிவு இல்லாதவர்கள் வேறு எதனைப் பெற்று இருந்தாலும் ஒன்றும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of wisdom over all material possessions. Those who have wisdom are considered to have everything, as wisdom guides them to acquire, protect, and use all other things rightly. Conversely, those who lack wisdom, even if they possess immense wealth or other resources, are deemed to have nothing because they cannot retain or use them properly. The contrast between 'உடையார்' (possessors) and 'இலர்' (those who have nothing) emphasizes that wisdom is the ultimate wealth.
